moment.text: Whenever he wanted to paint a picture, Wang Mo would first drink wine, and when he was sufficiently drunk, would splash the ink onto the painting surface.
moment.lead: The Tang-dynasty legend of the technique’s inventor, as told by Zhu Jingxuan:

moment.text: A Japanese zen monk, Sesshū Tōyō, traveled to china in 1468-1469 to study contemporary Ming painting and through his studies he created the Haboku style.

matters.text: This is why even the rocks and trees of Sesshu strike you with a sort of unearthly force, as if more real than reality.
